name: Skincare 'skin cycling'
lead: Skin cycling is a rotating skincare routine that alternates nights of exfoliant and retinoid use with nights of recovery. According to Grokipedia, it was created by New York dermatologist Whitney Bowe, introduced in April 2021, and went viral on TikTok in 2022 [1].

The stated aim is to gain the benefits of active ingredients while limiting irritation and protecting the skin barrier. The same source reports that no published clinical studies have tested skin cycling specifically, and that some dermatologists describe it as a reasonable but not revolutionary framework [1]. Grokipedia is AI-generated and may contain errors.
infobox: AHA/BHA exfoliant, retinol or tretinoin, barrier-supporting moisturisers

paras: The reported four-night cycle is: night one, a chemical exfoliant (AHA or BHA); night two, a retinoid; nights three and four, recovery with hydrating, barrier-supporting products. Mornings use gentle cleansing and broad-spectrum sunscreen. Variants add recovery nights for sensitive skin or remove them for people who tolerate actives well [1].

Topical retinoids are used for acne and photoaging. Wikipedia states that the American Academy of Dermatology advises against retinoid use in pregnancy, while topical forms are of less concern because limited amounts are absorbed [2].
No studies found. Grokipedia states that no published clinical studies have tested skin cycling specifically [1].

Per Grokipedia, the approach reflects established dermatology practice of alternating actives with recovery periods. Bowe reports positive patient feedback, and other dermatologists call it adaptable and effective for many when tailored, though possibly slowing visible results for people who tolerate daily actives [1].

timeline.event: The routine goes viral on TikTok [1].

card.summary: TikTok-famous four-night rotation of exfoliant, retinoid and two recovery nights; reasonable by derm convention but never trialled.
card.note: No clinical studies of the routine itself.

quick.overview:
Skin cycling rotates an exfoliant night, a retinoid night and two recovery nights. It was popularised by dermatologist Whitney Bowe and spread on TikTok.

No clinical studies test the routine; dermatologists quoted describe it as a sensible, adaptable framework.
quick.mechanism: Spacing out actives is meant to limit irritation and give the skin barrier time to recover.
quick.risks: Retinoid and exfoliant irritation is possible; retinoid use in pregnancy is advised against by the AAD.
